stories.headline: Unlocking Global Markets Through Student Entrepreneurship and Export Skills

stories.body:
Higher education institutions hold immense potential to shape the future of international trade, according to an opinion piece by Kabir Abdulsalam published in Premium Times. The discussion emphasizes that students do not need to wait until graduation to begin engaging with global markets.

The pathway to exporting spans across multiple academic disciplines and fields of study. For instance, a food science student possesses the foundational knowledge required to develop innovative, export-ready food products tailored for international consumers.

Creative disciplines also offer direct routes to international audiences. Fashion designers studying on campus have the capacity to build globally recognized clothing and leather brands straight out of their academic environments.

Meanwhile, technology and service sectors provide entirely digital avenues for global reach. Software developers can easily export digital solutions and technical services across borders without the physical logistics traditionally associated with international trade.

Students pursuing fields such as engineering, agriculture, accounting, logistics, marketing, and business administration are also uniquely positioned. Each of these disciplines equips learners with specialized skills that support different stages of the modern export value chain.

By encouraging entrepreneurial thinking and export readiness at the campus level, the educational system can help foster a new generation of global business leaders. Equipping students with these practical tools ultimately strengthens the broader economic landscape.
